title: I will ALWAYS be a sucker for a show that completely immerses you in ...
transcript: The sexiest show in New York right now is happening in a lavish basement in Chelsea. It's a new musical called memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen. It's based on a Japanese manga and is the first Japanese manga to be adapted into an English language musical. It takes place in Paris inside of a club known as the Night Egg where we follow a sex worker named Colette as she writes down her fantasies, her confessions and the stories of the men and women she encounters every night and finds her own voice in the process. Now this theatre is in the former McKittrick Hotel where sleep no more was and is completely transformed. It's opulent and in the round and everyone sitting at ables, you immediately feel like you've entered this dark, decadent underground palace. It's not interactive in any way. You do not like engage with the actors, but the staging is very immersive. This is a Duncan Cheek musical. He suddenly and very tragically passed away right before this show started previews. His music has meant so much to me over the years and this score is unmistakably him, dark, aking and pulsing with life. Genuinely getting to hear Sophia and Caruso wail a Duncan Sheik song is worth the price of admission. I think she's one of the best vocalists on the planet. Really unbelievable in this. Now, memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen is still in previews. It doesn't officially open until October 15th. But if you love the decadent Theatricality of on route, the intimacy and the immersiveness of cabaret at the Kitkat Club or the World Building and the complicated dynamics of great comment. This is very much up your alley. Memoirs of amorous Gentlemen is currently scheduled to run through January 3rd. I'm so glad I got to experience it. Thank you for everything, Duncan.
